title: Simultaneous coordinate quotients and parameters in a blowup algebra
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d\geq1$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ be a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and $j\in J$. Write $L=J\setminus\{j\}$ and set $$A=R[u_i\mid i\in L]/(t_i-t_j u_i\mid i\in L).$$ Coefficients and variables in quotient rings are denoted by the same symbols. Assume that $A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Use the labelled coordinate family $\mathcal C=(t_j,(u_i)_{i\in L},(t_k)_{k\notin J})$; labels remain distinct. For $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$, $U\subseteq L$ and $K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\setminus J$, put $$Q_{\epsilon,U,K}=\epsilon(t_j)+(u_i:i\in U)+(t_k:k\in K),\qquad c=\epsilon+|U|+|K|,$$ where $0(t_j)$ means the zero ideal. Then $A/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}$ is a regular ring. For every prime ideal $P\supseteq Q_{\epsilon,U,K}$, its localization satisfies $$A_P/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}A_P\text{ is regular local},\qquad \dim A_P=\dim(A_P/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}A_P)+c$$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. At every prime $P\subset A$, all members of $\mathcal C$ lying in $P$, with their displayed labels, simultaneously occur as distinct members of one regular system of parameters of $A_P$. Thus a chosen coordinate intersection is empty near $P$ if one chosen coordinate is a unit there, and otherwise its local equations are part of such a system and have codimension $c$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121: the vanishing chart coordinates form part of local regular parameters; all simultaneous coordinate quotients and their codimensions (also Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118)

proof.text: First fix $U,K$ and put $T=U\cup K$, $R_T=R/(t_h:h\in T)$, and $D=d-|T|$. Reorder the original regular parameters with the indices in $T$ first. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $R_T$ is regular local of dimension $D$. The images of the remaining $D$ parameters generate its maximal ideal, hence form a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Here $j\notin T$, so $D\ge1$. Put $L'=L\setminus U$ and $B=R_T[v_i\mid i\in L']/(t_i-t_jv_i:i\in L')$. There is an isomorphism $A/Q_{0,U,K}\cong B$: send coefficients to their classes in $R_T$, send $u_i$ to zero for $i\in U$ and to $v_i$ otherwise. The old relations with $i\in U$ map to $t_i=0$, and the others to the displayed relations. Conversely $R\to A/Q_{0,U,K}$ kills $t_k$ for $k\in K$ and $t_i=t_ju_i$ for $i\in U$, so factors through $R_T$; send each $v_i$ to $u_i$. The composites fix coefficients and variables, so are identities by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, coordinate substitutions; algebra.tex Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] to $R_T$ with its remaining parameter list, nonempty centre index set $J\setminus U$ and distinguished index $j$ (reindex the finite list if necessary). Its chart is precisely $B$ from Step 1. Thus $B$, and hence $A/Q_{0,U,K}$, is Noetherian and regular; multiplication by $t_j$ on $B$ is injective, and $B[1/t_j]\cong R_T[1/t_j]$ sends $v_i$ to $t_i/t_j$. This includes $L'=\varnothing$, when $B=R_T$. None of this invokes the coordinate-quotient lemma being proved.

source.place: VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, the same standard parameter chart over a parameter quotient.

proof.text: For $\epsilon=1$ put $C=R/(t_h:h\in J\cup K)$. The same reordered-parameter application of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes $C$ regular local of dimension $d-|J|-|K|$. We have $A/Q_{1,U,K}\cong C[v_i:i\in L\setminus U]$. Define the forward map by the coefficient quotient, $u_i\mapsto0$ for $i\in U$, $u_i\mapsto v_i$ otherwise. It kills $t_j$, every $t_k$ for $k\in K$, and every relation $t_i-t_ju_i$. For the inverse, the coefficient map to $A/Q_{1,U,K}$ kills all $t_i=t_ju_i$ with $i\in L$ as well as $t_j$ and $t_K$, so factors through $C$; take $v_i\mapsto u_i$. Both composites fix the ring generators by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. A regular local ring is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]; thus [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] makes this polynomial ring regular, including dimension zero and no variables. Together with Step 2 this proves the global regularity assertion for both values of $\epsilon$.

source.place: VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, exceptional coordinate quotient; Stacks Tags 00NQ and 0AFS; polynomial regularity Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: We next verify injectivity of each remaining nonexceptional coordinate on $A/Q_{0,U,K}=B$. The injection by $t_j$ from Step 2 implies $B\to B[1/t_j]$ is injective: the fraction relation in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] says an element mapping to zero is killed by some $t_j^n$, and repeated cancellation gives zero. For $i\in L\setminus U$, the element $t_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R_T$: put this remaining parameter first and apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] and [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. It remains a nonzerodivisor in $R_T[1/t_j]$: if $t_i x/t_j^n=0$, then $t_j^m t_i x=0$ in $R_T$ for some $m$, so $t_j^m x=0$ by cancellation of $t_i$, and $x/t_j^n=0$. Multiplication by the unit $t_j^{-1}$ preserves injectivity, so $v_i=t_i/t_j$ is a nonzerodivisor there, and hence on the subring $B$. Exactly the same fraction calculation for a remaining $k\notin J\cup K$, putting $t_k$ first in $R_T$, proves multiplication by $t_k$ is injective on $B$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM); Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction relation. Expanded injectivity calculation on every partial coordinate quotient.

proof.text: Order the chosen $u_U$ and $t_K$ in any order and, if $\epsilon=1$, append $t_j$ last. After every prefix not containing $t_j$, Step 1 identifies its quotient with the chart associated to exactly the indices already removed. Step 4 proves injectivity of the next nonexceptional coordinate; Step 2 proves injectivity of the final $t_j$ if present. Thus this length-$c$ list is weakly regular, meaning precisely the injectivity condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Fix $P\supseteq Q_{\epsilon,U,K}$. All entries lie in $P$, so [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] gives a regular sequence of length $c$ in $S=A_P$. By the assumed regularity of $A$, $S$ is Noetherian regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The localization-quotient isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] gives $S/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}S\cong(A/Q_{\epsilon,U,K})_{P/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}}$. Steps 2-3 and [def-weil-regular-scheme] show this ring is regular local. Applying [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] to the displayed regular sequence in $S$ now gives $\dim S=\dim(S/Q_{\epsilon,U,K}S)+c$. Regular local dimensions are finite, so this is also the ordinary integer equality asserted.

At an arbitrary prime $P$, choose exactly the labels of $\mathcal C$ whose elements lie in $P$; they determine some $\epsilon,U,K$ and a list $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in\mathfrak n$, where $(S,\mathfrak n)=(A_P,PA_P)$. By Step 5, $\overline S=S/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ is regular local of dimension $e=\dim S-c$. Choose a regular parameter system $\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_e$ in $\overline S$ and lift it to $y_1,\ldots,y_e\in\mathfrak n$. Then $(f_1,\ldots,f_c,y_1,\ldots,y_e)=\mathfrak n$: for any $z\in\mathfrak n$, express its image as $\sum\bar a_i\bar y_i$, lift the coefficients, and note $z-\sum a_i y_i\in(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. The displayed list has length $c+e=\dim S$, so is a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], with each chosen label assigned its own first position. For $c=0$ this simply chooses a parameter system of $S$; for $e=0$ no lifts are required.

source.place: Tag 00NU (lemma-regular-mod-x), proof by lifting maximal-ideal generators; here the dimension equality has already been proved in Step 5.

proof.text: If a selected coordinate $f$ is outside $P$, it is invertible on the basic open $D(f)$ containing $P$. Indeed in $A[1/f]$ its inverse is $1/f$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; its coordinate ideal there is the unit ideal, so that intersection is empty on this neighbourhood. Otherwise Step 6 puts every selected coordinate into a single regular parameter system, and Step 5 gives its codimension $c$. Keeping all labels throughout Steps 5-6 proves simultaneous containment, rather than making separate choices for different coordinates.

lean.statement: theorem coordinate_quotients_and_parameters {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (t : Fin d → R) (ht : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn t)) (J : Finset (Fin d)) (hJ : J.Nonempty) (j : Fin d) (hj : j ∈ J) [IsRegularRing (traceChartRing t J j)] : (∀ S : Finset (Option ((J.erase j) ⊕ {k : Fin d // k ∉ J})), IsRegularRing (traceChartRing t J j ⧸ coordinateIdeal t J j S) ∧ ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (traceChartRing t J j), coordinateIdeal t J j S ≤ p.asIdeal → IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal ⧸ (coordinateIdeal t J j S).map (algebraMap (traceChartRing t J j) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))) ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) = ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal ⧸ (coordinateIdeal t J j S).map (algebraMap (traceChartRing t J j) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))) + (S.card : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (traceChartRing t J j), ∃ s : List (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal), IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters s ∧ ∃ f : {a : Option ((J.erase j) ⊕ {k : Fin d // k ∉ J}) // coordinate t J j a ∈ p.asIdeal} → Fin s.length, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ a, s.get (f a) = algebraMap (traceChartRing t J j) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (coordinate t J j a.val)) ∧ (∀ (S : Finset (Option ((J.erase j) ⊕ {k : Fin d // k ∉ J}))) (p : PrimeSpectrum (traceChartRing t J j)), (∃ a ∈ S, coordinate t J j a ∉ p.asIdeal) → ∃ a ∈ S, coordinate t J j a ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ (coordinateIdeal t J j S).map (algebraMap (traceChartRing t J j) (Localization.Away (coordinate t J j a))) = ⊤)
